title: Alexander Isak return will boost Liverpool but Alisson faces ‘longer’ period out, Arne Slot says
content:
Arne Slot believes the return of record signing Alexander Isak will give Liverpool a significant boost during the run-in but Alisson is facing another extended spell on the sidelines.

The Swedish striker is on the brink of a comeback after three months out with a broken leg. Slot must decide whether to use him off the bench in Saturday’s FA Cup quarter-final at Manchester City or hold him back for next Wednesday’s Champions League quarter-final first leg away to Paris Saint-Germain.

“Alex (Isak) trained with us yesterday for the first time after exactly 101 days out,” Slot said. “It will definitely be too fast to expect him in the starting line up (against City).

“It will take a bit of time to give him a lot of minutes but we will make sure we do the right thing in terms of building him up. It is a very good thing to have him on the training ground again. It will be even better to have him available for games.”

Asked if Isak could feature against City as a substitute, Slot added: “It is a difficult one because we don’t play a normal game. What I mean is that it could go to extra time. That makes it more complicated if we think he can only play 10 minutes and bring him on and then it goes to extra time. Maybe a few minutes but let’s wait and see how he is today and how he feels about it himself.”

Mohamed Salah is set to start at the Etihad after recovering from a groin injury and Jeremie Frimpong is also fit with the scans clear after he went off in discomfort for the Netherlands against Ecuador on Tuesday.

However, Alisson will be absent and the Brazilian goalkeeper is certain to miss both legs of the PSG tie after suffering another hamstring injury before the international break.

“Ali will be out for a bit longer. Towards the end of the season we expect him to be fit,” Slot said.

It’s a crunch fortnight for Slot’s side as they attempt to salvage something from a turbulent campaign. They are still competing for silverware on two fronts and are locked in a battle for the top-five Premier League finish which would secure Champions League qualification.

Isak required a long time to get up to speed after missing pre-season prior to completing a £125million move to Anfield from Newcastle United in September. But Liverpool desperately need him to provide an injection of firepower in the coming weeks and ease the burden on Hugo Ekitike.

“It wasn’t only that Alex missed pre-season, he also missed the end of Newcastle’s season and didn’t go with the national team,” Slot explained. “What’s realistic? Our rehab staff did a great job, especially when I look at Alex now compared to where he was before he got injured. I see a player that is much stronger, physically in a much better place.

“But going from 100 days off to the intensity of the Premier League and the end phase of the Champions League where the opposition you face is even harder…… what’s realistic? That’s difficult to say.

“But I am really happy that I have at least a No 9 again available behind Hugo or together with Hugo so that is already a positive thing. Next season after a proper pre-season we can expect more from him but the way he is now is already a big step forward for us compared to what we had.”
